newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile to bar rallies for or against Cuba's Castro.
newsitem.headline: Chile to bar rallies for or against Cuba's Castro.

text.p: Chilean authorities, hoping to avert street disturbances at an Ibero-American summit next week, will not allow spontaneous rallies for or against Cuban leader Fidel Castro after he arrives on Saturday, President Eduardo Frei said on Tuesday.
"We're going to be very inflexible on this point," Frei told a news conference.
"We will not allow any demonstrations either in favor or against, except those that are strictly in line with the law and have a permit."

With 2,000 police in charge of security, Chile will receive the heads of state of 18 Latin American nations plus the prime ministers of Spain and Portugal for the annual summit on Sunday and Monday in the biggest international event in Chile's history.
Cuban exile groups and local anti-communists promised to demonstrate against Castro, due to arrive on Saturday, while leftists planned welcome rallies for him at every step of his two-day visit.

Cuban dissident Armando Valladares, a former U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Human Rights Commission, arrived in Chile this week and said the presidents should urge Castro to start a transition to democracy on the Caribbean island.

"I would ask these presidents for once to think of the people of Cuba who, for nearly 40 years, have been under this terrible dictatorship, and to criticize the situation that Cuba is in today," Valladares told a Monday news conference.
Some politicians in Frei's own center-left coalition government have said the summit delegates should press Castro for political reforms to Cuba's one-party system.
Frei said Castro, usually the center of media attention at such summits, would get the same treatment as any other president.

"The president of Cuba has been received at the five previous (Ibero-American) summits, and for that reason he will receive the same treatment as all the other heads of state," said Frei. "Our tradition has always been one of hospitality to visitors."
